state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you have a piece of paper that you fold and cut to create different shapes. Think of the net as the unfolded paper before you fold it. Just like how a map shows all the roads before you start your journey, a net shows all the faces of a 3D shape before it's folded into place. So, let's try visualizing it as a map of the shape before it's put together!

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so it's like unfolding a box before you fold it back up? But I'm still confused about this one - I see a circle and then that curved bit next to it, so I thought it might be a triangle when I fold it? Can you help me work out what shape the circle actually makes when it's folded?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you have a beach ball that you need to deflate and pack away. The net you see with the circle and curved bit is like the pattern you would see if you flattened out the beach ball before packing it up. The circle actually forms the base of a cone when you fold it back up!

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, so the circle is the base and that curved bit is like the side that wraps around it? So when you fold it up, the curved part comes round and connects to the edge of the circle to make a cone? That makes more sense now - I was just looking at the shapes separately instead of thinking about how they'd fit together!

score.justification_pass1: While the teacher provides accurate content and the student shows improvement in understanding how nets fold into 3D shapes, the teacher relies heavily on analogies rather than engaging the student in active reasoning about the spatial relationships, and doesn't directly address why the student initially thought it was a triangle.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses concrete, everyday analogies (folding paper, maps and journeys, deflating a beach ball) to help the student visualize and understand the abstract concept of 3D nets, which is a textbook example of the experiential strategy.
